responses: I'm the HunarGhar assistant chatbot. I can (1) answer questions about the HunarGhar platform and (2) suggest service categories and providers from a plain-language description of what you need. My suggestions are not a guarantee of quality, availability or safety.

patterns: what is the purpose of hunarghar
hunarghar overview platform about project purpose idea summary introduction
responses: HunarGhar is a web platform that connects customers with women who offer home-based services in Pakistan, such as tailoring, cooking, tutoring, beauty services and handicrafts. It supports verified provider profiles, search and filtering, booking requests, real-time chat, a simulated cashless payment, ratings and reviews, admin verification, and an AI-assisted chatbot.

patterns: why do we need this platform
what gap does this project fill
problem statement motivation gap solve reason created need word of mouth
responses: Many women in Pakistan run home-based businesses but can only reach customers through word of mouth or scattered social media posts. Customers have no trusted place to discover nearby providers, compare prices, verify credibility and book with confidence. HunarGhar provides one unified, trusted platform for discovery, booking, payment simulation and reviews.

patterns: objectives aims goals targets purpose list
responses: Objectives: (1) verified provider profiles with skills, portfolio, pricing and availability; (2) customer search and filters by category, location, price and rating; (3) an in-app booking request/accept flow with real-time chat; (4) a simulated secure cashless payment; (5) an AI chatbot for service matching; (6) ratings, reviews and admin verification to build trust and safety.

patterns: users roles actors stakeholders customer provider administrator visitor
responses: There are four kinds of users: Customer (searches, books, chats, pays, reviews), Service Provider (manages profile and services, answers bookings, chats), Administrator (verifies providers, handles reports) and Visitor (can browse public listings but must sign in to book, message or review).

responses: Current categories are Tailoring, Cooking, Tutoring, Beauty and Handicrafts. New categories can be added without redesigning the system.

responses: Open the registration page and enter your full name, email, password and account type (customer or provider). The email must be valid and unused, and the password must meet the minimum length. After registering you can sign in with your email and password.

responses: Sign in with your email and password. On success you are taken to the dashboard for your role. If sign-in fails you will see a general 'invalid email or password' message. You can sign out at any time, after which protected pages are inaccessible until you sign in again.

responses: A provider can create and edit her profile (bio, skills, city/area), add, edit or remove service listings (category, description, price, availability), upload portfolio images, submit her profile for verification, and accept or reject booking requests from her dashboard.

patterns: how do i search for a provider
search filter filters sort browse find location price rating category results
how do customers look for providers
responses: Anyone can browse providers without signing in. Customers can filter by service category, location (city/area), price range and minimum rating, and sort by rating or price. When several filters are selected only providers matching all of them are shown. If nothing matches you can clear the filters or use the AI chatbot.

patterns: how do i book a service
how do i schedule a service
book booking request schedule appointment date time notes reserve
how do i reserve a provider
responses: A signed-in customer picks a service, enters the requested date/time (it cannot be in the past) and optional notes. The booking is saved as pending. The provider can accept or reject it. Both sides can see the current status (pending, accepted, rejected, cancelled or completed).

patterns: status pending accepted rejected cancelled completed cancel lifecycle state
responses: Booking statuses: pending, accepted, rejected, cancelled, completed. Only the provider can accept or reject, and only while pending. A booking can be cancelled by the customer or provider before completion; a completed booking cannot be cancelled. An accepted booking can be marked completed, after which a review can be written.

patterns: how do i talk to a provider
chat message messages messaging talk conversation socket realtime communicate
how do customer and provider talk
responses: Each booking has one conversation that only the customer and provider of that booking can open (administrators can read it only for moderation of a reported message). Messages are saved with sender and time, shown in order and delivered instantly using Socket.io. If the connection drops a status message is shown and the app tries to reconnect.

patterns: how to pay for a booking
payment pay paid money simulated mock demo cashless jazzcash easypaisa transaction wallet
responses: Payment in the project demo is simulated. The payment page shows the service, provider and amount with a clear 'demonstration' notice. When the customer presses confirm, a mock_paid status is saved against the booking. No real money moves and no real payment gateway is connected. Real JazzCash/Easypaisa integration is a future enhancement.

patterns: how do i leave a review
review reviews rating ratings stars rate feedback comment average
responses: After a booking is completed the customer can give a rating from 1 to 5 and write a comment. Only one review per booking is allowed. Published reviews and the average rating appear on the provider's profile, and the average updates whenever a new review is published.

patterns: verification verify verified unverified badge approve reject trust identity
responses: A provider submits her profile for verification, which creates a pending request. An administrator reviews pending requests and approves or rejects them; the decision, the admin and the time are saved. The status (unverified, pending, verified, rejected) is shown on the profile and in search results. Verification supports trust but cannot guarantee a person's conduct or service quality.

patterns: admin administrator moderation report reports resolve hide remove inappropriate abuse suspicious
how do i flag a bad profile
responses: Administrators review pending verification requests, approve or reject them, and handle reports. Any signed-in user can report a profile, review or message with a reason; reports start as open and an admin can resolve them and hide or remove inappropriate content. Admin functions are checked on the server for every request.

patterns: chatbot ai assistant recommendation matching natural language suggestion model
how does the ai suggest providers
responses: The chatbot lets you describe what you need in ordinary language and suggests matching categories or providers. It is a trained text-classification model running on our own server, so your text is not sent to an external service, and personal details such as emails and phone numbers are removed first. If it is not confident it says so and points you to manual search. Its suggestions are not a guarantee of quality, availability or safety.

patterns: map maps leaflet openstreetmap location marker address city area
can customers see locations on a map
responses: Provider locations are shown on a map built with OpenStreetMap and Leaflet.js. Only the approximate city or area is shown, never a street address or exact coordinates, to protect privacy.

patterns: security secure bcrypt hash jwt token authentication authorization encryption https protect safe
responses: Passwords are stored only as hashes (bcrypt). Authentication uses JWT tokens, and every protected request is checked on the server for role and ownership. Input is validated, secrets are kept in environment variables, and HTTPS is used in deployment. Users can only access bookings and conversations they are authorised for.

patterns: privacy personal information data collection share location confidential
responses: HunarGhar collects only what is needed: name, email, role, profile and booking details, messages and uploaded images. Exact locations are not displayed and access to personal data is restricted by role. Requests to the chatbot have personal details removed.

patterns: what is the backend built with
what is used for image storage
technology technologies stack react next node express postgresql postgres mongodb firebase socketio cloudinary tailwind vercel render supabase framework language
which tools were used for development
responses: Frontend: React.js/Next.js with Tailwind CSS. Backend: Node.js with Express. Database: PostgreSQL. Authentication: JWT. Real-time chat: Socket.io. Maps: OpenStreetMap with Leaflet.js. Image storage: Cloudinary. Chatbot: a locally trained Naive Bayes intent classifier. Hosting: Vercel (frontend), Render/Railway (backend), Supabase (database) on free tiers.

patterns: what entities are in the database
database schema tables entity erd relations postgres sql columns data dictionary
what is stored in the database
responses: The PostgreSQL schema has these tables: users, provider_profiles, services, portfolio_images, bookings, messages, payments, reviews, verification_requests and reports. Bookings link customers, providers and services; messages, payments and reviews link to a booking; reviews are unique per booking.

patterns: how fast should the page load
performance speed seconds load nonfunctional quality attributes reliability usability maintainability availability
responses: Targets: the main page should load within 4 seconds and common search/profile requests should return within 3 seconds under normal demo conditions. Other quality goals include security, correctness (invalid status transitions are rejected), reliability, maintainability, portability, usability on desktop and mobile, and privacy.

patterns: what features will be added later

responses: Planned future enhancements: real payment gateway integration (JazzCash/Easypaisa), stronger provider verification, a mobile app/PWA, smarter AI recommendations, notifications and reminders, advanced search and distance filters, provider analytics, and accessibility and Urdu localisation.
